mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing, leading to increased economic activity, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate and high GDP growth indicates an easing monetary cycle with strong economic activity, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing cycle with strong growth
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods with high GDP growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment rate and high payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low unemployment and high payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in retail sales indicates increased consumer spending, leading to increased economic activity, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during periods of monetary easing.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high retail sales and monetary easing (t-test p > 0.05).
